info.description:
# Introduction
Public REST API for Flood Watch Ongkharak. The Go API is the public backend.

# Evidence and freshness
Keep OFFICIAL, COMMUNITY, and AI provenance distinct.
Availability data that is stale or unavailable is UNKNOWN, never SAFE.

# Authentication
Access tokens use JWT bearer authentication.
Refresh tokens are sent only in an HttpOnly cookie. The cookie uses the configured
SameSite Lax or Strict policy and Secure is enabled in production; refresh tokens
are never returned in response bodies. Phase 2 flood-domain collections are empty
until explicitly populated; no response implies current safe conditions. GUEST has
no persisted role; only USER and ADMIN accounts exist. Authentication is required
for the Phase 1 demonstration routes.

# Community reports
Phase 6 community reports are always COMMUNITY evidence. Only VERIFIED reports
and their images are public; an empty list never means SAFE. Submission time is
not a measured observation time. Pending reports are owner-editable, rejected
and verified reports are immutable, and an ADMIN cannot verify their own report.

# Alerts and realtime
Phase 7 alerts are created only by explicit structured rules; no threshold is
preconfigured. Public SSE transports versioned change notifications, not canonical
resource state. Redis outages do not roll back committed PostgreSQL data.

# Errors
Other auth failures use the ErrorResponse envelope (including 403 origin rejection,
415 unsupported media type, 429 rate limiting, and 500 infrastructure failure).

post.description: Sends a six-digit code to a valid supplied email without disclosing account eligibility. Unknown, disabled, and Google-only accounts cannot obtain a reset grant. Requires configured SMTP; never returns the OTP. A new accepted request invalidates the previous challenge and grant. Limited to one request per email per 60 seconds and five per hour, plus the direct-peer limit.

202.description: SMTP accepted the account-neutral email; this does not prove inbox delivery or that an eligible account exists. Response is not cacheable.

429.description: Email cooldown/hour cap (RECOVERY_RATE_LIMITED) or direct-peer cap (RATE_LIMITED). Retry later; Retry-After does not guarantee eligibility when the hourly cap remains exhausted.

500.description: Internal recovery failure without diagnostic details.

503.description: SMTP is disabled or delivery failed (RECOVERY_UNAVAILABLE). No fake success is returned.

post.description: Atomically consumes the grant, updates the Argon2id hash, revokes all refresh sessions, and increments the account authentication version so old access tokens fail. Does not log the user in.

Guest-accessible. `id` is a Redis stream cursor distinct from envelope `eventId`.
Reconnect with Last-Event-ID (or cursor query in browsers that cannot set headers).
`replay.reset` requires a full canonical REST refetch after an expired cursor or
bounded replay; initial subscription begins at the current stream tail.
Heartbeats are SSE comments. Delivery can be duplicated and has bounded retention.
Pending/private reports never appear; `report.verified` is the public signal.
